Marathon Petroleum stock fell 1.6% today to close at $367.99, capping a sharp five-day decline of 10.8% from its November 12 peak. The primary driver appears to be escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Iran has conducted direct military strikes on U.S. installations in Kuwait, extending a broader run of Gulf attacks that has damaged confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a reliable energy corridor, according to the IEA. While crude oil prices remain elevated around $90 per barrel, refinery utilization is high at 95.7%, refiners like MPC benefit most from stable supply chains and pricing. Disruption risk in a key oil transit route creates uncertainty about feedstock reliability and future margins, even if near-term crude prices haven't collapsed.

The sell-off also reflects a broader market reassessment of energy demand. Record diesel prices in the UK are driving inflation concerns, and there's growing chatter about massive electricity demand shifts ahead—data center power use could double by 2030 as AI booms—which could reshape longer-term energy consumption patterns in ways refiners are still pricing into their outlooks. The combination of geopolitical friction and demand-side unknowns has pushed the stock down over 2% in just two weeks.
